text:
jon_customer: Hey team — after upgrading to github.com/redwood/inference-go v0.9.2 we're seeing intermittent 504s on streaming completion calls. No other code changes. Happens every few minutes under moderate burst traffic.

jon_customer: Minimal repro: we create an http.Client with a custom Transport and call client.NewRequest(...) then sdk.Client.Do(ctx, req). Works for a while then 504s. Logs show both 'context canceled' and upstream 504s.

jon_customer: snippet:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 20,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // we use ctx for timeouts
// per-request
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := sdkClient.Call(ctx, req)
```

jon_customer: curl directly to the hosted endpoint doesn't exhibit the same 504s. Any ideas?

mia_support: Thanks @jon_customer — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a short log snippet showing the timestamps around a 504? Also which region and whether you're on Dedicated/Hosted?

jon_customer: Hosted, us-west-2. Log sample (redacted):
```
2025-09-01T15:02:41Z INFO request start id=abc123
2025-09-01T15:02:51Z WARN request error id=abc123 err="context canceled"
2025-09-01T15:02:51Z INFO retrying request id=abc123 attempt=2
2025-09-01T15:02:52Z ERROR request failed id=abc123 status=504 body="gateway timeout"
```

sam_sdk: Hey folks — a couple things to check. v0.9.2 changed the retry wrapper to reuse the provided http.Client but also adds an internal short-lived goroutine that can cancel a request on our retry timeout. If your per-request ctx is tight (10s) and our retry/backoff overlaps, you can see context canceled followed by a 504 from the server when the retry actually runs.

sam_sdk: Quick checks:
- Are you reusing the same http.Client/Transport across requests? Creating a new client per request + transport can exhaust sockets.
- IdleConnTimeout=30s is a bit low for high-reuse workloads — if the transport drops an idle connection right before reuse, the first request on that conn can fail and trigger retries.

sam_sdk: Workarounds we've seen help:
1) Reuse a single *http.Client and *http.Transport globally (package level).
2) Increase IdleConnTimeout to 90s+ and MaxIdleConnsPerHost to match concurrency.
3) Bump your per-request context timeout to > expected server time + retry budget, or disable SDK retries via Client.Options.RetryPolicy while testing.

sam_sdk: Example change:
```go
var defaultTransport = &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns:        500,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
var httpClient = &http.Client{Transport: defaultTransport}
// pass httpClient into sdk.NewClient(...)
```

dave_sre: Also flagging that when a client cancels a context, the server may still return a late 504 which gets logged — that explains the paired "context canceled" + "504" lines. The root cause is often the client-side connection reuse + server-side connection close timing.

jon_customer: OK will try making a package-level httpClient and bumping IdleConnTimeout. One question: is it safe to remove per-request context timeouts and rely on SDK retries? We need not to block forever.

sam_sdk: We recommend keeping a context timeout on the caller side but increasing it to account for retries. If you must keep a tight deadline, set Options.RetryPolicy to fewer retries or 0 so we don't attempt retries after your ctx is done. Eg: ClientOptions{RetryPolicy: sdk.RetryPolicy{MaxAttempts: 1}}

jon_customer: Applied the transport changes and set MaxAttempts=1 for now. After 30m under load the 504 spikes stopped. I'll monitor for a day and report back. Thanks.

mia_support: Great — thanks for the update. If you see anything, please paste tcpdump or netstat output and we can escalate to infra.

ci-bot: Deployed SDK patch v0.9.3-beta that includes a note in the README about reuse of http.Client and an opt-in which disables the internal retry wrapper via ClientOptions.DisableInternalRetries.

sam_sdk: We'll follow up with a small patch to make retry timing more conservative so it respects caller ctx deadlines earlier. Filed issue: #1248.

jon_customer: Confirmed stable after the changes. Appreciate the quick triage! :thumbsup:
